text: In modern software development, testing is essential for building reliable applications. Unit tests check individual functions or components in isolation, helping developers catch bugs early. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different modules work together correctly, such as a database communicating with the user interface. Many teams use test-driven development, where they write a failing test first, then write the minimum code to make it pass, and finally refactor. This approach encourages clear design and reduces wasted effort. Ultimately, a comprehensive testing strategy gives developers confidence. It means they can add new features or change existing code without constantly worrying about breaking something, and they can release updates more safely.
